questions.hint: A conjugate is formed by flipping the sign between two terms in a binomial surd expression (e.g. the conjugate of \\(a+\\sqrt{b}\\) is \\(a-\\sqrt{b}\\)). Multiplying a binomial surd by its conjugate uses \\((x+y)(x-y)=x^2-y^2\\) to eliminate the surd from the denominator.

steps.explain: A conjugate is formed by changing the sign between the two terms of a binomial. Identify the two terms of \(\sqrt{3}-1\): first term is \(\sqrt{3}\), second is \(1\).
Write the expression in the form \(a - b\). Note the sign between terms is a minus.
Apply the conjugate rule: change \(-\) to \(+\) to get the conjugate.
Verify: multiplying \(( \\sqrt{3}-1)(\\sqrt{3}+1) = 3-1 = 2\\), a rational number — confirming these are conjugates.

steps.explain: Identify the two terms of \(2\sqrt{5}+3\): first term is \(2\sqrt{5}\), second term is \(3\).
Write the expression in the form \(a + b\). Note the sign between terms is a plus.
Apply the conjugate rule: change \(+\) to \(-\) to get the conjugate.
Verify: \((2\\sqrt{5}+3)(2\\sqrt{5}-3) = 20 - 9 = 11\\), a rational number — confirming these are conjugates.

steps.explain: Identify the two terms of \(\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{2}\): first term is \(\sqrt{7}\), second term is \(\sqrt{2}\).
Note the sign between terms is a minus.
Apply the conjugate rule: change \(-\) to \(+\).
Verify: \((\\sqrt{7}-\\sqrt{2})(\\sqrt{7}+\\sqrt{2}) = 7-2 = 5\\), rational — confirming these are conjugates.

steps.explain: Identify the two terms of \(3\sqrt{11}+4\sqrt{6}\): first term is \(3\sqrt{11}\), second is \(4\sqrt{6}\).
Note the sign between terms is a plus.
Apply the conjugate rule: change \(+\) to \(-\).
Verify: \((3\\sqrt{11}+4\\sqrt{6})(3\\sqrt{11}-4\\sqrt{6}) = 99-96=3\\), rational — confirming conjugates.

questions.stem: Write down the result when the expression \\(\\sqrt{3}-1\\) is multiplied by its conjugate.
questions.hint: A conjugate is formed by flipping the sign between two terms in a binomial surd expression (e.g. the conjugate of \\(a+\\sqrt{b}\\) is \\(a-\\sqrt{b}\\)). Multiplying a binomial surd by its conjugate uses \\((x+y)(x-y)=x^2-y^2\\) to eliminate the surd from the denominator.

steps.explain: Write the expression \(\sqrt{3}-1\) and identify its conjugate: \(\sqrt{3}+1\).
Apply the difference of squares identity: \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2-b^2\). Identify \(a = \sqrt{3}\) and \(b = 1\).
Substitute the squared values into \(a^2 - b^2\).
Calculate the final result. Notice it is rational — no surds remain.
